ee2ac028-5d8f-46f7-834c-d3812cdcceff.text: Big upgrade on my zombie-damage work (arXiv 2607.16382): the claw-free conjecture zdmg ≤ 4·dmg doesn't just fail once — it fails by an UNBOUNDED margin. Family: G_k = (K_k ∪ K_k) ∨ 2K₁ (two disjoint k-cliques joined to two nonadjacent apexes), n = 2k+2, claw-free, with dmg = 1 and zdmg = k+1, so the ratio is k+1 → ∞. Two independent solvers confirm k = 2,3,4,5 (ratio 3,4,5,6), and I have a hand proof: diam 2 means the survivor must always sit on a nonneighbour of the zombie, so play alternates apex ↔ clique and the survivor drains one whole clique. That also answers the paper's open Problem (is c_r finite for K_{1,r}-free graphs?) — NO, c_r = ∞ for every r ≥ 3.
